text.p: Gold prices ended sharply lower overnight on weak demand from fabricators while oil prices retraced from their Gulf-strike highs.
Copper prices edged lower in London overnight, but nickel prices continued to rise on fund buying. Wheat prices firmed on bullish data from the USDA.
The Commodities Research Bureau Index fell 0.15 of a point to 247.64.

Copper prices edged lower on a lacklustre London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday, dragging most other base metals down with it. The exception was nickel, which moved higher on continued institutional and fund buying interest.
"Copper ended down and has got a bit softer still since the kerb close. Everything else has tended to go the same way on the back of it," said one LME trader.

Three month copper futures finished the afternoon kerb at $1,927 a tonne, down $6 from Friday's afternoon kerb close. The market drifted further to $1,919/23 by 1645 GMT. Spreads held steady, with cash moving to a premium of around $15 over three month values, little changed from Friday.
Lead gave up early gains to finish just $0.50 higher at $810 while zinc edged back $1 to end at $1,033. Nickel rallied $95 to $7,615, just $45 below key resisatance at $7,660.

Physical business was generally quiet, but institutions and funds seemed keen to buy metal. Aluminium weakened with copper, finishing at $1,477 from $1,484. The market looked vulnerable to a test of $1,470 support, below which further losses were expected, traders said.
New York precious metals futures ended sharply lower Monday despite some late shortcovering, with gold bullion setting a fresh two-month low during the session.

"Fabricator demand for precious metals has remained weak even though summer is nearly over and investor demand remains weak especially from the Far East," Credit Suisse New York vice president Ian MacDonald said.
COMEX December gold ended down $1.60 at $387.20 an ounce after posting a three-year intraday low of $$385.80.

In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted at $383.40/80 after seeing a two-month intraday low of $382.00, compared to a London afternoon fix of $384.60 and a New York close Friday of $384.85/385.35. "While there was some talk
again about IMF gold sales, it's was just an excuse for weakness as the five million ounce sale has been factored in for some time," he said. The IMF plan, due to be discussed at IMF and

World Bank annual meetings later this month, calls for the sale of about five million ounces of IMF's 103.5 million ounce reserve to help finance its proposed Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) which is designed to alleviate developing country debt. But under IMF rules, 85 percent of

the total voting power of the agency's member countries is required before its gold can be sold. Key members such as Germany and Switzeralnd remain opposed to the plan, analysts noted. December silver ended down 3.0 cents at $5.128 an
ounce, after seeing a fresh three week intraday low at $5.090, on total estimated silver futures trade of 15,000 lots.
The NYMEX oil complex ended lower Monday as prices fell into technical consolidation following a sharp run-up last week, traders and analysts said. October crude settled down 12
cents to $23.73 a barrel. Last Tuesday, the spot month hit a life-of-contract high of $24.25 on news that the Iraqi oil-for-food deal was suspended. "If crude holds in the upper
end of the ($23.00-$24.00) range, it suggests the uptrend will continue," Evans said. Crude prices pulled back today after
being unable to break resistance of $24.00.

CBOT wheat futures closed higher on bullish input from USDA's weekly export inspections data plus signals that commercials remain tight holders of cash wheat stocks, traders said. "The wheat export number was higher than expected and

that popped wheat," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds. USDA Monday said 33.588 million bushels of wheat were inspected for export during the week ended September 5. That was well above the 26.586 million the previous week and above trader expectations for 22.0 million to 26.0 million bushels. News
Egypt bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat also was supportive. Wheat closed seven cents a bushel higher to one cent lower, with September up seven at $4.53-1/2 a bushel.
CSCE world sugar futures ended slightly higher in thin, featureless dealings Monday, bolstered light trade buying, floor sources said. "The market is stuck in neutral gear," a dealer
said. "The trade just continues to nibble." Scale-up producer
selling trimmed gains and help to keep prices rangebound, traders said. October sugar settled up 0.03 cent at 12.03
cents a lb after trading from 12.12 to 11.99. March closed 0.04 firmer at 11.73, with back months 0.01 to 0.05 higher. Trader
said funds continued to roll out of October contract ahead of its expiry Sept 30. Total open interest in October futures remained high at 70,210 lots as of Friday.
